reason:
I confirm the finding. I ran no tests: it is a documentation finding, so the evidence is git reads of the branch.

Evidence on session/rich-steps:
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 opens with "Frozen 12 Sep. Changes after that are reviewed pull requests."
- Section 4 (lines 158-171) shows Step with top-level id, tool, title, state, startedAt, endedAt, cost, preview and childTaskIds.
- packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts on the branch has Step { taskId, index, kind, text, detail? }.
- In that file tool, cost and childTaskIds are under the optional detail. durationMs replaces startedAt and endedAt. rows and output are new. id, state, title and preview are absent.
- The diff stat for origin/main...session/rich-steps lists 20 files, and none is under docs/.
- origin/main sessions.ts line 27 has the comment that points to "docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4". A grep of the branch file for "ARCHITECTURE" or "§" returns nothing, so the branch deleted the pointer.

One part of the finding is overstated. The difference between section 4 and the code is older than this branch: main already had the four-field Step. The old comment explained that difference, because it said the richer step would come later and would only add fields. The branch does two new things:
1. It ships a richer step with a shape that section 4 does not describe: a nested detail, and a duration in place of a start time and an end time.
2. It removes the only sentence that connected the two files.

After the merge, a teammate who reads the "frozen" section 4 will write code against step.id, step.state and step.cost, and these fields do not exist. The steering owner is one example. Section 5 (step.full with stepId, step.content) and section 6 (streamText(stepId, delta)) also depend on a step id, and the contract has no step id.

Severity stays should-fix, not blocker. Nothing fails at runtime, the contract change is additive, and `npm run verify` does not check this. The fix is small, and either of these is enough:
- Update the Step block in section 4 to the shipped shape, and mark id, state and streaming as not yet landed.
- Restore a comment in sessions.ts that says which file is the truth.

The three points in the finding about what StepDetail leaves out for spec page 04 are true: there is no running state or start time for a live "run 2 m 41 s", and no step id. They are limits on scope, because the commit message calls itself "Step 2" of the page work. They are not defects of this commit. They belong in a follow-up note and must not block the merge.
